text:
Anya Kumar: quick alert 1: onboarding open-7b-int4-v3 -> we're seeing subtle token substitution after ~7k tokens in our longctx harness. Not repeating phrases exactly like before, more like single-token skew that accumulates. Anyone on?

Diego Ramos: on it. single-token skew could be rotation misapply or key-slot misalignment. Which rope variant? fused or per-head?

Anya Kumar: `--rope-mode=fused` in these runs. Command: `./eval_longctx.sh --model open-7b-int4-v3 --ctx 16384 --quant int4 --rope fused --batch 1 --seed 7`

Liu Chen: did you try fused vs scaled? fused has in-place interleaving math that sometimes interacts poorly with packed int4 kernels.

Anya Kumar: scaled runs look clean. Fused shows the drift. Dumped logits at divergence point: `step=186 token_idx=7124 top5: [0.42,0.21,0.08,0.06,0.05] -> next step top1 changed from 0.42 to 0.14 unexpectedly`

Sofie Hart: can you attach the key/val key checksum before+after prefill/inflight? Also which pack layout: we use nibble-pair little-endian or big-endian?

Anya Kumar: attaching small trace (pasted): `KV_CHKSUM_PREFILL=0x7f3a2d, KV_CHKSUM_INFLIGHT=0x7f3a2c` 1 mismatch. Layout: nibble-pair-le (current int4 packing).

Diego Ramos: 1-bit difference in checksum suggests a single-bit shift during pack/unpack or a rounding error in int4 kernel. Did the int4 pack change recently? Liu?

Liu Chen: yes, we switched to 2x4-bit pack stride optimization in commit 9f8c3 last week to reduce memory stride on interleaved shards. I ran microbench but not longctx. Could introduce carry when sequence length crosses word boundary.

Anya Kumar: repro matrix quick: int4/fused/interleaved -> skew; int4/fused/single -> skew but less frequent; int4/scaled/interleaved -> pass; float16/fused/interleaved -> pass. So it's int4+fused+interleave interaction.

Diego Ramos: hypothesis: pack code computes pack_index = (token_idx >> 1) - (token_idx >= boundary ? 1 : 0) (example) and boundary calc off-by-one at word boundary (word = 64 nibbles maybe). Let's add an assert that reconstructed nibbles == original for every pack/unpack roundtrip in prefill path.

Anya Kumar: added assert in dev build: `pack_roundtrip_assert FAILED at token 7124: orig=0xA unpacked=0x8` -> nibble lost high bit. That points to shift mask maybe using 0xF but apply >> instead of & after sign-extend.

Liu Chen: I found suspicious line in pack_kernel.cu: `packed_word |= ((val & 0xF) << ((i & 1) * 4));` should be `((i%2)*4)` but that's equivalent. More suspect: later we call atomicOr with a 32-bit lane but our packing uses 64-bit stores on some GPUs which can race. Are you seeing races in interleaved mode because multiple shards write into same 64-bit word?

Sofie Hart: good call. interleaved sharding maps different token indices from different ranks into adjacent nibbles in same 64-bit. With non-atomic 64-bit stores in pack path under int4 micro-optim, writes can overlap. We used to do per-nibble atomic updates but changed to wider stores for perf.

Anya Kumar: ran a run forcing atomic nibble writes (slower) -> fused/interleaved/int4 now stable for 50/50 seeds. That confirms race.

Diego Ramos: plan: revert wide-store micro-optim, add a vectorized atomic routine that does compare-and-swap loop for 64-bit but ensures nibble correctness, and add longctx soak. Also add a unit test that simulates concurrent packing across multiple writer threads with randomized token indices that share word boundaries.

Liu Chen: PR in progress: `fix/int4-pack-atomics` 1 switching to CAS loop. Bench run shows ~+0.8% CPU in prefill but token p99 unchanged.

ci-bot: CI started for fix/int4-pack-atomics 1 unit tests (packing_concurrency) running

Anya Kumar: local 1k-seed randomized sim -> no failures. Pushing to gated MR for CI-run. Also wrote an e2e longctx smoke with fused+interleaved+ctx=16384 -> 500 randomized seeds, no divergence so far.

Sofie Hart: excellent. After merge we'll schedule a 48h soak on dedicated pools and watch embedding/serving customers with long prompt workloads. Tagging @eng-sre for rollout window.

Diego Ramos: add a small telemetry metric for kv_prefill_pack_conflicts to surface any residual CAS retries so we can watch perf.

ci-bot: CI green for unit tests, smoke 500/500 passed, integration perf nominal. MR: https://git.internal/redwood/rlib/pull/4902

Anya Kumar: merging MR now. Will monitor next staging deployment (rolling) and open incident-lite if any customer anomalies. Thanks all.

Liu Chen: nice catch. we'll follow up with a short postmortem note and include the packing_concurrency test in our onboarding harness.

Anya Kumar: closing thread.
